authoredFrom: A `$ref` may name an IDENTITY the document declares (`$id` base URI / `$anchor` fragment) instead of a JSON Pointer into it. JSON Schema resolves that reference against the declared base and the declaration IS the object carrying the `$id`, whose qualified path this analyzer already publishes. Before the fix the raw string was published with `isExternal: true`, so the arbiter classified it `externalUnverified` (this lane's 4-edge `ext?` class on gql-graphql-mesh). The four expectRelationships pin the QUALIFIED PATH of the declaring object on each form (base identity, anchored identity, resource-relative identity, document-root identity), and the four forbidRelationships pin that the raw spelling is no longer an endpoint. Every entry is additive (`extra actual items are fine`), and forbidRelationships is the negative half: a fix that published BOTH the identity and the raw string would still fail this pin.

expectRelationships.note: base identity: the $ref names the $id declared by the object at definitions.PetDetails
anchored identity: the fragment names the $anchor declared on PetDetails.properties.id
resource-relative identity: the $id ends with an empty fragment and the $ref does not
a $ref INSIDE the PetDetails resource resolves against its own base, not the document root
document-root identity: the $id on the root object declares the module's own identity

forbidRelationships.note: the raw identity spelling must not be an endpoint any more
